item.title: Flash-Moe: Running a 397B Parameter Model on a Mac with 48GB RAM
item.description:

HN Discussion

Read Original Article

Top 8 Comments:

zozbot234:

The github page mentions that a naïve mmap approach is bottlenecked by per-page overhead. Can this be mitigated by setting up explicit "huge" pages? (2M using the CONT PTE feature if the "native" page size is 64k; or 512M using a PMD level block mapping.) Does macOS support this out of the box?

vilequeef:

Why so much RAM?

pdyc:

impressive, i wish someone takes a stab at using this technique on mobile gpu's even if it does not use storage it would still be a win. I am running llama.cpp on adreno 830 with oepncl and i am getting pathetic 2-3t/s for output tokens

bertili:

Very impressive! I wonder if there is a similar path for Linux using system memory instead of SSD? Hell, maybe even a case for the return of some kind of ROMs of weights?

JSR_FDED:

This is a very impressive result. If I understand correctly the bottleneck is the SSD in this architecture - the author seems to get almost 15GB/s - but I seem to remember the max b/w was about 8GB/s. What am I missing?

rvz:

The technical write up is great, but Mac users should not get too excited just yet on running 300B+ parameter models locally as the TPS isn't that good.

>...at 4.4+ tokens/second

That is even when it is using 4-bit quantization and it is still at that speed.

> The entire 209GB model streams from SSD through a custom Metal compute pipeline.

This is my main problem.

If I were to run this on a Mac SSD, 24/7 for heavy usage such as Openclaw, that is going to significantly reduce the lifetime of the SSD.

Can't imagine using this in the long term right now, but improvements will follow. Still a great write up anyways.

harshhhhhhhhh:

seems promising , this is the way , can someone benchmark this

item.title: Hormuz Minesweeper – Are you tired of winning?
Windows native app development is a mess
item.description:
I’m a Windows guy; I always have been. While I followed the Windows development ecosystem from the sidelines, my professional work never involved writing native Windows apps. 0 (2002) started out with Windows Forms.

HN Discussion

Read Original Article

Top 5 Comments:

ozim:

That is why everyone even Microsoft themselves does Electron.

Running with html/css/js has benefits it really is open and free development based on international standards and not locked into any single big tech.

delduca:

Best framework for this is Qt.

intrasight:

"So when I went to work on my app, I was astonished to find that twenty years after the release of WPF, the boilerplate had barely changed."

Such is the benefit and the curse, I guess, of having the Windows API being locked in the distant past for backwards compatibility.

I've always been surprised that Microsoft didn't do a full operating system refactor and provide a compatibility layer for running old binaries. Perhaps they figure it would be better to just transition everything to software as a service using web tech? But I just don't see how that strategy is gonna work long-term.

wolvoleo:

> And from what I can tell, neither are most developers. The Hacker News commentariat loves to bemoan the death of native apps. But given what a mess the Windows app platform is, I’ll pick the web stack any day, with Electron or Tauri to bridge down to the relevant Win32 APIs for OS integration.

Well yes as a user I prefer native apps for their performance. It's clearly a mess to develop native apps as the article shows. But as a user I don't see that problem. I do see ever worsening apps though. Like the total mess that is new outlook and teams.

ashwinnair99:

It has been a mess for 15 years and Microsoft keeps making it worse by adding new frameworks without retiring the old ones. Win32, WPF, WinUI, MAUI. Nobody knows which one to pick.

item.title: 'Miracle': Europe reconnects with lost spacecraft
item.description:
March 19, 2026 'Miracle': Europe reconnects with lost spacecraft edited by Andrew Zinin Editors' notes This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies. The Proba-3 mission blasted off from India in 2024. Key concepts Solar instrumentsArtificial satellitesSolar corona © 2026 AFP Citation: 'Miracle': Europe reconnects with lost spacecraft (2026, March 19) retrieved 22 March 2026 from https://phys.

HN Discussion

Read Original Article

Top 3 Comments:

tetris11:

> Proba-3, works just like a real solar eclipse. One spacecraft, which is roughly circular when viewed from the front, orbits closer to the sun, and its job is to block the bright parts of the sun, acting as the moon would in a real eclipse. It casts a shadow on a second probe that has a camera capable of photographing the resulting artificial eclipse.

> Having two separate spacecraft flying independently but in such a way that one casts a shadow on the other is a challenging task. But future missions depend on scientists figuring out how to make this precision choreography technology work, and so Proba-3 is a test.

Oh wow, they've potentially rescued this (very cool!) mission for both probes

graemep:

The European Space Agency, not 'Europe'. Just as annoying as calling the EU Europe, and calling both Europe despite different membership is just confusing.

touwer:

I'm glad that this site at least left ~10% of the screen on my phone to read the article, next to all banners and newsletter ads. It's not 5%, great!
